messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automated page: latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. p95=710ms, p99=2680ms, streaming stalls flagged. Severity: P1. Paging oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: acknowledged. I'm on it. First check: any deploys/rollouts in the last 30m?
michael: no deploys. I see a sharp tail spike starting at 03:12 UTC on the serving cluster. Streaming connections show stalls (clients hang while the token stream resumes later).
katie: infra side seeing GPU node health anomalies in the same timeframe. Node gpu-wn-17 showing repeated ECC correctable errors (CE) and thermal warnings.
alex: routing shows traffic was evenly distributed; a subset of requests routed to gpu-wn-17 had p99 ~ 4s while others were fine. Looks like localized hardware issue and not a global autoscaler event.
ryan: customer-impact: jess, any external reports?
jess: CS confirmed two enterprise customers reported slower response times and timeouts on streaming. They're escalating. I'll send a heads-up and share the incident channel.
oncall-sre: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain gpu-wn-17 2) failover traffic to spare GPU pool 3) enable model fallback to quantized variant for streaming-heavy routes to lower tail latency. Executing now. :hammer:

oncall-sre: running `kubectl cordon gpu-wn-17 && kubectl drain gpu-wn-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
michael: grabbing GPU logs: attaching snippet.
```
[ 03:11:58 ] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=2543 SCHED_STATE=0 Gpu hangs.
[ 03:12:01 ] nvidia: GPU 0: Corrected ECC error detected. total=42
[ 03:12:05 ] thermal: GPU temp threshold exceeded, throttling clocks on GPU 0
```

katie: also seeing kernel dmesg lines: `gpu 0000:65:00.0: GPU reset due to scheduler timeout` — node is flaky. Recommending to mark as degraded and avoid re-scheduling heavy streaming pods on that host until we replace or move GPUs.

alex: rolling routing rule change: routing policy -> prefer gpu-spare-pool for /v1/generate for next 20m. Will reduce per-request latency impact.
oncall-sre: applied route fallback to `g4-quantized-v1` on the edge for streaming sessions and lowered concurrency on GPU pool to reduce tail amplification.
ryan: throttling note — if ECC CE count climbs it triggers hardware thermal mitigation on this board, causing clock down and periodic stalls; that matches the stalls seen in streaming.
michael: quick mitigation done: 1) drained node, 2) restarted serving on GPU spare pool, 3) temporarily enabled CPU fallback for low-priority jobs.
jess: alerted affected customers: status page updated, CS outreach started. Customers asked for ETA; we told them 2 hours while we investigate hardware.
oncall-sre: monitoring: p95 back to ~320ms, p99 trending down to ~800ms after failover and fallback. Streaming stall rates dropped ~90%. :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: next steps: capture full node logs, mark gpu-wn-17 as DECOMMISSION_PENDING, escalate to HW vendor for ECC/thermal failure, schedule hot-swap replacement. Also run eviction and revalidate for any pods that touched the node.
katie: filing vendor ticket now, attaching ECC counts, dmesg, `nvidia-smi -q` output. Ticket #VEND-4521.

michael: postmortem actions I've added: - add specific alert for rising corrected ECC rate threshold, - add automated routing shift when node-level ECC > X, - add streaming stall synthetic tests to detect tail stalls earlier.

ryan: ops note: consider adding a transient model variant with lower memory footprint for streaming to avoid exacerbating stalls if a single node starts misbehaving.
jess: logging CS follow-up tasks and customer communication timeline.
oncall-sre: handing over to morning oncall: @alex please take follow-ups and coordinate hardware replacement, @katie please own the vendor ticket updates. I'll update the incident on-call handoff log and mark P1 -> P2 after stabilization.
alex: ack, will coordinate. Thanks everyone. :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation implemented, partial recovery observed. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes or on major change.

oncall-sre: final note before handoff — root cause likely a degrading GPU causing thermal-triggered throttling after ECC CE spike. This produced intermittent stalls and long tail latencies for streaming. We'll keep the node offline until vendor replacement.

michael: saving traces and perf profiles to the incident bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1932104567/`
katie: vendor ticket updated with logs and schedule for physical replacement tomorrow 09:00 PT.

jess: CS notified customers that we routed them away from the impacted hosts and are replacing hardware; next status in 2h.

oncall-sre: closing on-call loop, handing to morning triage. Postmortem to be drafted, include mitigation timeline, customer impact, and detection gaps. :memo:
